# Cross-Exchange Liquidity Commentary – 2026-07-30

The liquidity hierarchy divides sharply into three tiers. The North American leaders—Nasdaq 100 and NYSE—dominate on all metrics: Nasdaq's 0.0025% per $1M ILLIQ and 0.7933% AR spread are unmatched, while NYSE's 0.6553% spread and $240.2M comparable volume underpin its #2 rank. The Asian and European mid-pack—Tokyo Stock Exchange, Euronext, SIX Swiss Exchange, and Hong Kong Stock Exchange—cluster between 0.0301% and 0.0457% per $1M ILLIQ, though Tokyo's elevated 3.8152% turnover ratio suggests concentrated trading in fewer constituents. A notable divergence emerges at Euronext, which posts a tight 0.5422% AR spread yet carries a middling 0.0301% per $1M ILLIQ, indicating information costs dominate over pure spread width there. The laggards—Korea Exchange, Xetra, and London Stock Exchange—suffer either elevated ILLIQ (Korea's 0.1558% per $1M), wide spreads (Korea's 1.6434% AR spread), or both. Korea Exchange's combination of poor metrics across all dimensions and minimal $24.0M comparable volume signals structural liquidity constraints for international participants.
